title: Molecular Basis of Selectivity in Human Elastin-Binding Protein toward Elastin Peptides and Galactosugars
authors: Zeynep Pinar Haslak; Nicolas Belloy; Laurent Debelle; Manuel Dauchez; Stéphanie Baud
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接与MD模拟研究弹性蛋白结合蛋白与肽段的结合模式，属广义蛋白-肽互作而非TF-DNA体系，但物理模拟方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA互作建模，故给5分。
abstract: Elastin-derived peptides (EDPs) modulate key cellular processes through binding to the elastin-binding protein (EBP), yet the molecular basis underlying their differential activities remains unclear. In this study, we combined systematic molecular docking with duplicate 1 μs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the binding modes and interaction networks of biologically active (LGTIPG, PGAIPG) and inactive (VVGPGA, VPVGGA, GGVPG) elastin-derived peptides (EDPs) within the V32 pocket of EBP. Our results reveal two partially overlapping functional regions within the V32 pocket: residues 98–114, preferentially engaged by biologically active peptides and galactosugars, and residues 83–104, primarily utilized by inactive peptides. This supports a model in which active peptides and galactosugars share a common region, while inactive peptides preferentially occupy an adjacent, partially overlapping subregion, challenging the notion of entirely separate EBP binding sites. Active peptides formed strong, persistent interactions, particularly through D98 and E99, whereas inactive peptides relied primarily on salt bridges with E137 and hydrogen bonds with S101. MM/PBSA binding free energies were in full agreement with experimental activity trends, indicating that binding affinity and pocket preference jointly determine biological activity. Notably, although type VIII β-turns are traditionally linked to EDP bioactivity, the peptides remained predominantly extended when bound to EBP, highlighting that binding-site selection and interaction networks, rather than β-turn formation, govern peptide activity. The surface residues P233 and I234 appeared as potential mediators of EBP’s interactions with Neu-1 and PPCA within the elastin receptor complex, supporting previous findings.
abstract_zh: 弹性蛋白衍生肽（EDPs）通过结合弹性蛋白结合蛋白（EBP）调节关键细胞过程，然而其差异活性背后的分子基础仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们结合系统性分子对接与重复1微秒分子动力学（MD）模拟，表征了生物活性（LGTIPG、PGAIPG）和非活性（VVGPGA、VPVGGA、GGVPG）弹性蛋白衍生肽（EDPs）在EBP V32口袋内的结合模式及相互作用网络。我们的结果揭示了V32口袋内两个部分重叠的功能区域：残基98–114，优先被生物活性肽和半乳糖类占据，以及残基83–104，主要被非活性肽利用。这支持了一个模型，即活性肽和半乳糖类共享一个共同区域，而非活性肽优先占据相邻且部分重叠的子区域，挑战了EBP完全独立结合位点的观点。活性肽形成强且持久的相互作用，特别是通过D98和E99，而非活性肽主要依赖与E137的盐桥和与S101的氢键。MM/PBSA结合自由能与实验活性趋势完全一致，表明结合亲和力和口袋偏好共同决定生物活性。值得注意的是，尽管VIII型β-转角传统上与EDP生物活性相关，但肽在结合EBP时主要保持伸展构象，强调结合位点选择和相互作用网络而非β-转角形成主导肽活性。表面残基P233和I234作为EBP与Neu-1和PPCA在弹性蛋白受体复合物中相互作用的潜在介导者出现，支持了先前的研究发现。
